communications.subject: New Hampshire Right to Know Law Request: Parole Board Member Terms and Salaries (New Hampshire Adult Parole Board)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Hampshire Right to Know Law, I hereby request the following records:

-the current term expiration date (month, day, and year) for each parole board member
-the annual salary / total compensation for each parole board member for 2026 

I am making this request for research purposes and am not a journalist.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jacob Wourms

communications.subject: RE: New Hampshire Right to Know Law Request: Parole Board Member Terms and Salaries (New Hampshire Adult Parole Board)
communications.communication:
Good afternoon Mr. Wourms,

The information you requested is as follows:

Term expiration date for current Parole Board members
Lynne Blankenbeker, Chairperson -September 16, 2030
Ronald Bessette, Vice-Chairperson-July 1, 2028
Eric Kulberg-September 29, 2031
Tricia Thompson-September 29, 2027
Christopher Pingree-July 8, 2031

The Salaries are set by statute (NH RSA 651-A:3—shown at the bottom of this email).  The Chairperson is a full-time state employee on the Unclassified Wage Scale as Grade GG, which is noted below in the screenshot from the NH Department of Administrative Services website.
[cid:image002.png@01DD616C.9B540540]

The remaining Board members receive an annual stipend of $30,000 except for the Vice Chairperson, who receives an annual stipend of $40,000.

And so you are aware, all of this information is public knowledge and available online.  I imagine you are not aware of where to look for the information, so I do not mind giving it to you with the areas that it can be found.  If you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact me.  Have a great day.


TITLE LXII
CRIMINAL CODE
CHAPTER 651-A
PAROLE OF PRISONERS
Section 651-A:3
    651-A:3 Adult Parole Board; Establishment; Procedures. –
I. There shall be an adult parole board with members as set forth in paragraph II. The members of the board shall be appointed by the governor with the consent of the council for staggered terms of 5 years or until their successors are appointed. No member shall serve more than 2 consecutive terms. A vacancy on the board shall be filled for the unexpired term. The chairperson of the adult parole board may appoint a member who previously served on the adult parole board whose term has expired to sit on a hearing panel when illness, conflict of interest, or unavailability result in only 2 members being available for a scheduled hearing. The compensation for such member appointed shall be $300 per day.
II. The composition of the board shall be as follows:
(a) Two attorneys who are members of the New Hampshire bar in good standing and who are in active status.
(b) Three additional members, to include:
(1) One member with law enforcement or corrections experience, either current or former.
(2) One member with criminal justice experience, which may be direct employment experience, current or former, in some capacity within the criminal justice system, or postsecondary school teaching, scholarship, and research pertaining to the criminal justice system.
(3) One at-large member without any categorical designation.
III. The governor shall designate one member as chairperson. The salary of the chairperson shall be that established in RSA 94:1-a as grade GG, with appropriate step to be determined in accordance the provisions of RSA 94:1-d. The chairperson shall designate one other member to serve as vice chairperson who shall serve as chairperson in the chairperson's absence. The vice chairperson shall receive an annual stipend of $40,000 to be paid in equal installments on each state employee pay period date. In the case of a revocation hearing an attorney of the board shall be present at the hearing. Board members, except for the chairperson and the vice chairperson, shall be paid an annual stipend of $30,000, to be paid in equal installments on each state employee pay period date. Board members shall be paid mileage at the state employee rate while engaged in parole hearings or administrative meetings.
IV. The board shall hold at least 36 days of parole hearings and 36 days of parole revocation hearings each year and may hold more hearings as necessary. Each parole and parole revocation hearing shall be held by a hearing panel consisting of exactly 3 members of the board. The board shall establish operating procedures which provide for rotation of board members among hearing panels.
V. In the event of a pandemic or other extraordinary occurrence declared an emergency by the governor that results in restricted movement or quarantining of inmates at any New Hampshire state prison facility, the parole board may conduct all hearings via teleconference or other video conference technology.
Source. 1983, 461:16. 1994, 305:2. 1995, 257:3. 2015, 194:1, eff. July 1, 2015. 2021, 91:126, eff. July 1, 2021. 2022, 260:2, eff. June 24, 2022. 2023, 134:1, 2, eff. June 30, 2023.

title: Edward Samuel Miller

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Edward Samuel Miller
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

The personnel file of former FBI Assistant Director Edward Samuel Miller, including file 67-HQ-45116. Proof of death is not required as he has an entry in the Dead List under "Miller, E.S.". According to previously released records, Miller's EOD date was September 29, 1950 and his retirement date was July 15, 1974.

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. This is also to include any responsive records held in offsite locations, such as the Alexandria Records Center. Please include both investigatory and non-investigatory records in your search. If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Paul Galante

title: Nebraska Public Records Request — Lincoln Police ALPR/LPR Records — January 1, 2023–Present

communications.subject: Nebraska Public Records Act Request: Nebraska Public Records Request — Lincoln Police ALPR/LPR Records — January 1, 2023–Present
communications.communication:
Dear City of Lincoln Records Custodian:

Pursuant to the Nebraska Public Records Act, Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 84-712 through 84-712.09, I request copies of the following existing records held by the Lincoln Police Department, City of Lincoln Police Records, City Attorney, Purchasing/Finance, IT, or any other City office that maintains responsive records.

Please search for records created, received, or maintained from January 1, 2023 through the date this request is processed concerning automatic license plate readers, automated license plate readers, automatic license plate recognition, license plate recognition, ALPR, LPR, Axon, Flock, Motorola, or “plate reader.”

Please provide:

All current and superseded ALPR/LPR policies, general orders, standard operating procedures, privacy policies, retention schedules, field guides, training materials, audit procedures, and policy-revision or approval records.

All annual ALPR/LPR practice and usage reports, attachments, corrections, and related correspondence prepared or submitted under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-3206.

All contracts, subscription agreements, statements of work, purchase orders, amendments, renewals, invoices, payment records, grant applications, grant awards, grant reimbursements, procurement records, bid materials, vendor proposals, selection memoranda, and vendor correspondence concerning ALPR/LPR equipment or services.

A current and historical inventory of ALPR/LPR equipment, including each device’s vendor, model, asset or system identifier, fixed or mobile designation, assigned vehicle or installation location, and installation, removal, replacement, or reassignment dates.

For fixed installations, all existing site-location records in the most specific non-exempt form maintained by the City, including street address, intersection, site identifier, map, GIS layer/export, installation plan, work order, pole/cabinet reference, or location approval record.

All existing aggregate or de-identified reports, dashboards, exports, statistics, audits, and access-review records concerning ALPR/LPR scans, alerts, confirmed matches, non-correlating matches, manual queries, user access, searches, exports, retention/deletion, and information sharing with other agencies.

All memoranda of understanding, data-sharing agreements, access agreements, interagency correspondence, vendor data-processing terms, cybersecurity/security assessments, privacy reviews, and system-integration records concerning ALPR/LPR information.

All complaints, internal reviews, policy-compliance reviews, misuse investigations, discipline or corrective-action records, and audit findings concerning ALPR/LPR access, use, dissemination, retention, or sharing. Please redact protected personal, investigative, or disciplinary information as necessary rather than withholding entire responsive records.

I am not requesting raw captured plate data, individual license plate numbers, raw images, or other data excluded from disclosure by Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-3209. To the extent any responsive record contains exempt information, please redact only the exempt portion and release all reasonably segregable non-exempt material.

Please provide records electronically by email or download link. Please provide structured records, including spreadsheets, reports, GIS data, and exported data, in their native or reasonably accessible machine-readable form when maintained in that form.

I am a Nebraska resident. Please notify me before incurring fees exceeding $50. If any portion of this request is likely to involve significant review time or cost, please provide an itemized estimate and identify the record categories or search terms responsible, so I may prioritize or narrow the request.

If any records are withheld in whole or in part, please provide a written response identifying the statutory basis for each withholding and release all reasonably segregable portions. If another City office is the custodian of responsive records, please forward this request or identify the appropriate custodian.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 4 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jeff Geiger

title: Flock Safety ALPR Systems Communications and Access

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Systems Communications and Access
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) User account audit logs documenting each time a department account has conducted a search or taken another action on the department's Flock Safety ALPR system from 1/1/2024 until the date this request is processed. Flock audit logs are retained indefinitely and contain metadata including, but not limited to: the date of the search, the time of the search, the search term/rules, and the user conducting the search. The audit logs are recorded in a database so I ask that you provide it to me as a .csv, .xls, or other database filetype.
2) Audit logs documenting the access reason for each time a department account has conducted a search on the department's Flock Safety ALPR system from 1/1/2024 until the date this request is processed. The access policy of SFPD for the Flock Safety ALPR system requires a "valid reason". If this valid reason is not recorded anywhere, please indicate as such. If there are audit logs with information regarding ongoing cases and therefore they cannot be provided, please indicate the count of the logs not provided for that reason, and provide the remaining logs that do not have information regarding ongoing cases. Otherwise, if logs contain information that cannot be publicly shared, please redact the information, and provide a reason for the redaction.
3) The names of the hot lists/watch lists used with Flock Safety automated license plate readers (ALPRs)  from 1/1/2024 until the date this request is processed
4) The names of all the agencies with which data is shared with through the Flock Safety ALPR system  from 1/1/2024 until the date this request is processed
5) The names of all the agencies from which data is received through the Flock Safety ALPR system  from 1/1/2024 until the date this request is processed
6) All agreements will local homeowner associations or private business or individuals for access to Flock Safety systems
7) All procurement documents related to Flock Safety
8) All Right-of-Way Installation Permits  relating to the Flock ALPRs
9)  Correspondence (emails, letters, memoranda) discussing installation, operating procedures, presentations, and policy relating to the use and deployment of Flock ALPRs
10) SFPD Internal operating procedures, presentations, and policy relating to the use and deployment of Flock ALPRs
11) Correspondence (emails, letters, memoranda) between SFPD personnel and Flock personnel relating to the purchase, installation, or usage of the ALPRs. Flock's email domain is "flocksafety.com". You may de-duplicate emails as needed in case Flock sends out newsletters or emails to multiple SFPD members. 

In the event that you determine certain records or portions of records are exempt from disclosure, I ask that you provide a detailed explanation of the records or portions of records being withheld and the statutory exemptions under which they are being withheld.
In the event that you determine SFPD does not handle or maintain certain records or portions of records, please indicate which office or department does.

I am requesting these records as a journalist in order to write articles in the public interest about the operations of a government agency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Austin Theriault

title: Information Regarding Md. Criminal Law Code § 9-804 (Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services)

communications.subject: Maryland Public Information Act Request: Information Regarding Md. Criminal Law Code § 9-804 (Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Unless otherwise specified, I am requesting data covering the five-year period:
1. The total number of individuals charged under Md. Criminal Law Code § 9-804 — including charges brought under subsections (a) (participation in a criminal organization), (b) (receipt or investment of criminal proceeds), (c) (acquisition of enterprise or property), and (d) (conspiracy) — broken down by subsection and by year for the past five years.
2. The racial and gender demographics of all individuals charged under Md. Criminal Law Code § 9-804 during that period, disaggregated by year and by subsection to the extent available.
3. Conviction rates for individuals charged under Md. Criminal Law Code § 9-804, including the number and percentage of cases resolved by conviction, acquittal, dismissal, nolle prosequi, or other disposition, broken down by year.
4. The number of individuals currently in the custody of the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services whose sentence includes a conviction under Md. Criminal Law Code § 9-804, including any cases charged under the enhanced penalty provision of § 9-804(e) (death of a victim) or as a second or subsequent offense under § 9-804(f)(2).
5. The number of cases over the past five years in which a charge under Md. Criminal Law Code § 9-804 was included in the initial charging instrument — indictment, criminal information, or delinquency petition as required under § 9-804(h) — but was subsequently dropped or reduced as part of a negotiated plea, broken down by year.
6. The average sentence length in cases where a § 9-804 charge was reduced or dismissed through a plea agreement, compared with the average sentence length in cases where the charge was carried through to conviction and sentencing, broken down by year to the extent available. Please include data on whether sentences were imposed consecutively or concurrently with underlying offense sentences, consistent with § 9-804(f)(2).
7. The age distribution — including mean age, median age, and full age range — of individuals charged under Md. Criminal Law Code § 9-804 over the past five years, including any cases in which the underlying conduct involved a juvenile act as referenced in § 9-804(a)(2).
The average total sentence length for the underlying predicate offense alone, compared with the average total sentence for the underlying offense combined with a § 9-804 charge, for cases resolved during the past five years.
8. The number of cases in which a § 9-804 charge was applied involving: (a) juveniles tried as adults in circuit court; or (b) delinquency petitions in juvenile court proceedings, over the past five years.
9. For defendants charged under Md. Criminal Law Code § 9-804 over the past five years: the number represented by the Office of the Public Defender versus private counsel, along with corresponding conviction rates and average sentence lengths for each group.

Andrew  Free

RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2025-ICFO-47866 
 
Dear Requester: 

This acknowledges receipt of your 7/8/2025, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), for records showing the name, government email address, and work phone number for each Deportation Officer, Supervisory Detention and Deportation Office, Assistant Field Office Director, Acting Field Office Director, and Field Office Director for the Columbus, Cleveland, and Cincinnati ICE ERO Sub-Offices (which are housed within the Detroit Field Office) for the period beginning January 20, 2025.  Your request was received in this office on 7/8/2025. 

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you’re able to narrow the scope of your request please contact our office. Narrowing the scope may speed up the search process. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. 

Provisions of the FOIA allow us to recover part of the cost of complying with your request.  We shall charge you for records in accordance with the DHS Interim FOIA regulations as they apply to non-commercial requesters.  As a non-commercial requester, you will be charged 10 cents per page for duplication; the first 100 pages are free, as are the first two hours of search time, after which you will pay the per quarter-hour rate ($4.00 for clerical personnel, $7.00 for professional personnel, $10.25 for managerial personnel) of the searcher.  We will construe the submission of your request as an agreement to pay up to $25.00. You will be contacted before any further fees are accrued. 

We have queried the appropriate program offices within ICE for responsive records. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for determination of releasability. Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request. 

If you have any questions, please contact FOIA Public Liaison, Daniel Edgington at 500 12th Street, SW, Washington DC 20536 or (866) 633-1182. Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974.  You may contact OGIS as follows:  Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448. 

Your request has been assigned reference number 2025-ICFO-47866. Please use this number in future correspondence. 

Sincerely, 

ICE FOIA Office 
Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Freedom of Information Act Office 
500 12th Street, S.W., Stop 5009 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5009

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #2026-ICFO-26574
communications.communication:
Dear Counselor and Staff,

I have received your categorical denial of my records request, dated May 7, 2026, regarding ICE FOIA Request 2026-ICFO-26574. Please accept this correspondence as a formal administrative appeal of that determination.

Your agency's blanket withholding of all responsive records under FOIA Exemptions 6 and 7(C) is, in my view, facially inconsistent with established Supreme Court precedent and the statutory intent of the Freedom of Information Act. I believe my request must be granted, in part or in whole, based on the following grounds:

1. The categorical denial of all responsive documents is unusually broad and effectively serves a primary interest of protecting the Department of Homeland Security and ICE from public scrutiny, rather than protecting legitimate privacy. It is legally untenable to assert that not a single responsive record or component thereof can be reasonably segregated and released. On this basis alone, a blanket, non-segregated withholding fails to satisfy the agency's statutory requirements.

2. The core justification of this denial rests upon the supposed privacy interests of the deportees transferred to the Centro de Confinamiento del Terrorismo (CECOT) complex. However, the agency has placed itself in an irreconcilable double-bind. ICE cannot simultaneously claim these individuals received sufficient administrative or judicial due process to warrant removal to a notorious foreign high-security detention facility, while concurrently claiming they retain an expectation of privacy so absolute that their very names must remain shielded from public record. If these individuals were processed and removed through official channels, that operation ipso facto implies a finalized, public administrative action by the United States government. Therefore, protection from "public misassociation" or the stigma of "alleged criminal activity" cannot logically serve as a valid baseline for a blanket denial.

3. The agency has fundamentally failed to meet its burden of proof in demonstrating that the privacy interests at stake "clearly outweigh" the overwhelming public interest in disclosure. Under U.S. DOJ v. Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, 489 U.S. 749 (1989), the core public interest under FOIA is uniquely served when records shed light on "what their government is up to." The transfer of individuals to a foreign mega-prison complex is an official, high-stakes administrative operation executed by the United States government. The American public has an undeniable, legitimate interest in knowing the operational parameters, scope, and identities involved in these official actions to hold government actors accountable. Furthermore, per John Doe Agency v. John Doe Corp., 493 U.S. 146 (1989), the Supreme Court has repeatedly stressed that disclosure, not secrecy, is the dominant objective of the Act. Categorically withholding all identities under the guise of an "unwarranted invasion of personal privacy" misapplies the balancing test. Because these individuals are subject to completed, formal government tracking and official foreign transfers, this matter is distinctly removed from the purely private personnel or medical records that Exemptions 6 and 7(C) were designed to protect.

While I maintain that a total categorical denial is structurally and legally invalid in this case, I am entirely open to a constructive, good-faith discussion regarding the reasonable scope of documentation to be released. This includes exploring appropriate line-by-line redactions if specific, acute safety concerns exist for certain individuals, provided the agency fulfills its obligation to release all segregable, non-exempt information.

Thank you. I look forward to your timely determination.

Sincerely,
Longform Letter

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. section 552) and the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. section 263a et seq.), this is a request for records in the custody of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS), Survey and Certification Group, Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) program.

REQUESTED RECORDS:

1. All CLIA certification letters, certificates of accreditation, and certificates of compliance issued to the following University of California clinical laboratories, from 1 January 2018 through the present:

   a. UC Davis Medical Center Clinical Laboratory, Sacramento, CA
   b. UC Davis Health Point-of-Care Testing sites
   c. UC Davis Testing Laboratory (if separately CLIA-certified)

2. CMS-2567 (Statement of Deficiencies) forms and any CMS-2567-related correspondence for each of the above laboratories for all inspection, re-inspection, and complaint investigation surveys conducted from 1 January 2020 through the present.

3. All CLIA waiver applications, provisional certifications, and any exception or waiver granted to UC Davis clinical laboratories during the COVID-19 public health emergency.

4. Any records of CLIA sanctions, adverse actions, limitation of certification, suspension, or revocation involving any UC clinical laboratory, including any pending actions.

5. Any reports of validation surveys, complaint surveys, or follow-up surveys involving UC clinical laboratories conducted by CMS or its deemed accrediting organizations.

TIME PERIOD: 1 January 2018 through the present.
FORMAT: Electronic copies.
FEE WAIVER: This request is made in the public interest. I request a waiver of all search and duplication fees under 45 C.F.R. section 5.43 because disclosure of the requested information is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations and activities of the government.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Daniel Friedman

title: MPSE Workforce and Provider data for Churn Analysis

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: MPSE Workforce and Provider data for Churn Analysis
communications.communication:
Dear Data Practices Compliance Official,

This is a formal request under the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act (MGDPA), Minn. Stat. § 13.03, for public data regarding individual provider enrollment and agency affiliations within the Minnesota Provider Screening and Enrollment (MPSE) system.

1. Request for Remote Inspection

Under Minn. Stat. § 13.03, Subd. 3, I am exercising my right to inspect public data. As inspection is free of charge, I am requesting access to these records in the MPSE in their original digital format.

Reasonable Accommodation: Due to intersecting access barriers related to a qualified disability, I am requesting a reasonable accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Title II.

Strict adherence to a standard physical office environment creates a barrier to my access. Specifically, I require accessible system fonts and a specialized, non-standard ergonomic environment (including custom seating and positioning supports) to review materials at length. As these specific necessary environmental modifications are not feasible to replicate in a standard public government office on a shared terminal, I am requesting access to inspect the public data elements in situ with database tools remotely (via remote desktop, secure VPN, or a read-only digital portal).

This accommodation allows me to utilize my own adaptive workstation to review the material effectively and equitably.

This data is required for a public-interest analysis of provider retention. We are investigating whether a reported 250% turnover rate indicates that case managers are leaving the field before reaching the 24-month cadence of interactive disability-led training sessions with DHS partners, or if they are simply migrating between providers.

Data Requested

I am requesting access to a list of all individual case managers and providers enrolled to provide services at any point between January 2015 and December 2025, including the duration of their enrollment associated with each provider.

To facilitate an efficient remote inspection, please ensure a minimum of the following data points are accessible:

    Individual's Full Name

    Individual's State Provider Number (UMPI)

    Individual's National Provider Number (NPI)

    Agency Name (Employer) (Affiliation Records (MPSE-0603))

    Agency's Provider Number (NPI or UMPI) 

    Enrollment Start Date (per agency) (Enrollment History (MPSE-0604))

    Enrollment End Date (per agency; blank if currently enrolled)

If possible, I would like to be have access to the all public headers, fields and tables in the dataset  Along with the data dictionaries in order to facilitate accurate analysis.

Format and Collaboration

While I am requesting remote inspection to avoid the unnecessary fees and physical barriers, I would prefer to review this in a database. If that is infeasible a SQL dump or export to spreadsheet format (CSV or XLSX) or monthly snapshots similar to the NPI files would be an acceptably alternative allowing me to derive the needed relationships in the data.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

As this work is for a non-commercial, public benefit, I respectfully request a full fee waiver for any copies I may ultimately require after my initial inspection.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

If any of your team members are interested in our findings on churn rate, I would be more than happy to share the finished analysis.

Thank you for your assistance in ensuring this process remains accessible.

Best regards,

Sincerely,

Jonathan Murray | (Please use name/Any Pronouns) 
**Principal, Strategic Systems Innovation Lead, Social Infrastructure & Interdependence** 
* I run on Criptime so it may take a while to respond. Please follow up if I've missed your e-mail, especially if it's urgent.

communications.communication:
Good afternoon, 

Following up on my MNDPA request and the request for payment for data access. 

The request specifically avoids asking DHS create new data, only for it to provide access to the public data in the databases segregated from information protected under the Minnesota Data Practices Act.

I understand the barriers that presents when the data is currently held within databases. I will need to use database tools either remotely or on on a MNDHS or MNIT machine.
The request offered of providing copies as a less burdensome way to comply with the obligations of the MNDPA in lieu of direct inspection.

I am reiterating my request to either have accessible remote access to the data directly or for copies to be provided free of charge. I am familiar with SQL and am happy to work with raw datasets and databases.

It's understandable that the DHS would like to avoid incurring costs. I believe providing access and working with me and others from the disability community to research the patterns the data will show, will greatly benefit the state of Minnesota through savings in case management & HCBS costs.

This isn't without precedent the Department of Health & DHS partnered with Elder Family Voices for related datasets and are providing ongoing technical support and data access for Elder Care IQ. https://eldercareiq.org/home

Elder care IQ is viewed as necessary because as "those vulnerable" we haven't had the agency, autonomy and authority ourselves to prevent abuses from happening to us and to stop them when they do. 

You can start to change that by taking this first step in partnering to create a disability lead and run disability data lab in MN. A place & platform on which  those of us who have already reached our disabled futures can work with Allies, Researchers, journalists, Policymakers and government officials all understand the disabled future we share. 

Until DHS buys into that vision. I would appreciate if you could provide access to the data free of charge as obligations under the MNDPA require.

Open roads and their skies,

Jonathan

title: Louis O. Giuffrida

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Louis O. Giuffrida
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records relating to, mentioning, or generated as a result of investigation of Louis Onorato Giuffrida (October 2, 1920 – November 20, 2012), who served as director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency from May 1981 to September 1985, being forced to resign amid mounting accusations of fraud, waste, and abuse. Proof of death is not required as his death was widely reported: http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/middletownpress/obituary.aspx?n=louis-o-giuffrida&pid=161812525#fbLoggedOut

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Paul Galante

Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks--simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Complex requests are further divided into medium, large, and extra-large sub-tracks based upon request size.  Simple track requests typically require the least amount of time to process.  Currently, simple track cases average approximately 104 days from the date of receipt for processing.  Our complex requests in the medium processing track are currently averaging 853 days, large processing track are currently averaging approximately 1,786 days, and extra-large processing track are currently averaging 2,500 days for processing.

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Untitled (San Diego Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting incident-level crime data for a research project comparing neighborhood-level crime across large US cities. I am asking for the same kind of extract many departments already publish through their open data portals.

Records requested. One row per reported offense, for offenses occurring between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2025, with these fields:

the incident, case or report number
the date the offense occurred
the offense description, and the offense code if you have one
the location of the offense, as latitude and longitude

Offense fields. Whatever your system already stores is fine. Something along the lines of NIBRS offense codes and descriptions is ideal, but please do not translate, recode or reclassify anything on my behalf. I am not asking you to do any work beyond exporting the fields as they sit. If your records hold more than one offense description or classification per record (for example a local code, a UCR or NIBRS code, and a plain-text description), please include all of them rather than choosing between them.

Location. If coordinates cannot be released, I will accept a block-level address instead - either "4200 BLOCK OF WYOMING ST" or an address with the house number masked to the hundred block, for example "42XX WYOMING ST". I am not asking for exact street addresses. Several large departments publish location in exactly this masked form, and it is sufficient for my purposes.

No personal information is requested. I am not asking for the name, address, date of birth, race, sex, age or any other identifying detail of any victim, witness, suspect, arrestee or officer. Please withhold all such fields. I am asking only for what the offense was, when it happened, and roughly where.

Format. CSV, or any delimited or database export your records system produces. One file for the whole period is easiest, but annual files are fine.

Cost. Please send me a written estimate before incurring any charge above $50.

If any part of this cannot be released, please release the rest and tell me what was withheld and why.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jonathan Mummolo

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting the flight path information related to any operations that occurred over or within 0.25 Statute Miles of 10 N Virginia Street Reno, 89501 between the dates of 07/10/2026 and 07/23/2026. The minimum data needed is:
- Minimum operating altitude within that radius
- Maximum operating altitude within that radius
- The UAS platform used (i.e. Skydio X10, BRINC Responder, etc.)
- System attachments equipped during operations (i.e. parachute, deployable floatation device, etc.)

An export of the flight logs is acceptable if this request as stated would require the creation of new documents. These flight logs are easily downloaded from the Fleet Management page of the respective fleet software. Data about the purpose of the flights may be anonymized, and this data can be filtered prior to export to ensure it is responsive only to the requested area and dates.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Daniel Jenkins

I have reached out via phone as well, but want to share this resource across to the Records Division. I understand the cited reason for delaying responding to this request is staffing constraints. Following the instructions in this article shared by Skydio, all requested records can be easily filtered and gathered with all requested information contained in that data set:

https://support.skydio.com/hc/en-us/articles/4402745384475-How-to-use-Fleet-Manager-in-Skydio-Cloud

The ease of use of this tool, and the extremely limited scope of the request should not require 2 months to provide. This request does not require the generation of any additional records, as these flights should already be logged and stored as mandated by the Certificate of Authorization or Waiver with the FAA that these operations occur under. This information can be requested by the FAA at any time, and must be stored to be compliant with FAA regulations, meaning that no new records should be required to be produced.

It is hard to believe that staffing issues are this significant a constraint when the Reno PD accounts for more than a third of the city spending. If action is not taken soon, a judicial remedy will be required as permitted under NRS 239.011.

I look forward to receiving the requested information promptly.

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under 
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com), 
exchanged with any Vancouver Public Schools District email account, alias, or internal 
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, 
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's 
available archival retention window.



TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and 
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives 
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of 
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.



LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal 
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is 
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings 
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals, 
and generalized policy or administrative discussions. 

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege 
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions 
may be withheld.



MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5) 
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Kung Fu Joe

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Audit logs dating back to January 1, 2026 for searches of any part of the Flock Safety system dating from the initial contract by government employees, private entities operating on behalf of the government, and/or unauthorized searches of the system by any party.

2. Official policy documents that show when and how the Flock Safety system may and/or may not be used.

3. Records of all alleged occurances of nonpermissible searches of Flock Safety systems to include the search criteria, the system(s) searched, the name of the individual that made the search, the stated reason(s) for the search, the current employment status of the one(s) alleged to have misused the system, and a copy of all disciplinary proceedings and the disposition of such proceedings that occurred as a result of the alleged misuse of the system.

4. A list of all criminal charges filed on or after January 1, 2026 where the data from Flock Safety has been admitted into evidence. This list need only include the venue for the case, the docket number, the associated law enforcement agency, the agency's case number(s) associated with the charges, the date the case was filed,  and the disposition status of the case (if available).

5. Financial records that disclose the amount of money disbursed to Flock Safety, Inc. since January 1, 2026.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. Given the volume of this records request, I would prefer the request filled electronically by USB flash drive if available, or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Nicholas Squires

All amendments, addenda, renewals, extensions, replacement agreements, and change orders associated with the contract.
All exhibits, schedules, scopes of work, service-level requirements, performance standards, route or fleet requirements, and other incorporated documents.
All pricing, rate sheets, payment terms, fuel-cost provisions, escalation formulas, incentives, credits, and other compensation-related terms.
All provisions or attachments addressing insurance, indemnification, bonding, data access, cybersecurity, student safety, reporting, records retention, subcontractors, audit rights, termination, and renewal options.

The requested date range is January 1, 2014 through the date this request is processed. If the District maintains multiple agreements or contract versions during that period, please provide each responsive version rather than only the most recent document.

Please provide the records by email or electronic download. If the District does not maintain a requested record, please identify the office or entity believed to maintain it, if known.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning, relating to, or generated as a result of investigation or inquiry of Irving Brown (November 20, 1911 - Feburary 10, 1989), a prominent labor leader and anti-communist activist. Proof of death is not required as his date of birth was over 100 years ago. Cross-references to Brown can likely be found in records on:

-Thomas Wardell Braden
-David Dubinsky
-Jay Lovestone
-Walter Reuther
-Victor Reuther

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. This is also to include any responsive records held in offsite locations, such as the Alexandria Records Center. Please include both investigatory and non-investigatory records in your search. If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Paul Galante

have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the

title: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Cecil County Sheriff's Office)

communications.subject: Maryland Public Information Act Request: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Cecil County Sheriff's Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I am hereby requesting access to the records listed below and held by the Cecil County Sheriff's Office.

1)	Any policies, procedures, protocols, and/or written guidance for the use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) by Cecil County Sheriff's Office. This request includes, but is not limited to policies setting forth permitted and prohibited uses for ALPRs and rules regarding who may and may not use this technology.

2)	Information about which people and agencies have access to images, videos, and raw data sets generated by ALPR systems monitored or maintained by Cecil County Sheriff's Office, under what circumstances these individuals have access to the above-mentioned data, and what information must be entered about any data requests. The list of agencies includes, but is not limited to, parking and traffic enforcement agencies, and other law enforcement agencies.

3)	Policies, procedures and information regarding Cecil County Sheriff's Office data retention and data purging practices for ALPR systems, including  Cecil County Sheriff's Office policies regarding handling images, videos, and raw data sets.

4)	Information about Cecil County Sheriff's Office audits or other procedures used to assure compliance with the above requirements.

5)	Information regarding the training that Cecil County Sheriff's Office personnel must undergo to use ALPRs, if any.

6)	ALPR training materials provided to Cecil County Sheriff's Office.

7)	Product and user manuals for all ALPR software and hardware possessed or used by Cecil County Sheriff's Office.

8)	The name of all ALPR vendors, ALPR software systems, and ALPR hardware currently used by Cecil County Sheriff's Office or by third party who make the information available to Cecil County Sheriff's Office. Hardware includes fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile devices. Software systems include optical character recognition and artificial intelligence capabilities.

9)	Description of how targets (aka “hot lists”) are shared with ALPR systems and monitored, including the sources for these data feeds.

10)	A list and map of locations where fixed-location ALPRs are currently located within Cecil County Sheriff's Office’s jurisdiction.

11)	The number of ALPR devices operated by the agency for the following categories: fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile ALPRs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, please disclose total charges in advance of fulfilling the request. Alternatively, please consider waiving any fees, pursuant to § 4-206(e)(2)(ii) of the General Provisions Article, as this request is on behalf of individuals served by the Maryland Office of the Public Defender, a state government agency, which solely serves indigent citizens of Maryland. As a result, my request for the above-listed public records is in the public interest. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available, or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jeff Gilleran
Chief Attorney
Forensics Division
Office of the Public Defender
6 St. Paul St., Suite 1508
Baltimore, MD 21202
(410) 804-7107
jeffrey.gilleran@maryland.gov

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Organized Retail Crime Task Force: Auror
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the Organized Retail Crime Theft Task Force announced on June 23, 2022, specifically concerning the implementation, use, and discussion of Auror's crime intelligence platform.

1. All contracts, MOUs, RFPs, or service agreements between the AG's Office and Auror Inc. (auror.co) dated June 23, 2022, to present
1a. Amendments, scope-of-work documents, or SLA agreements related to Auror's services
1b. Invoices, payment receipts, or procurement documents for Auror software/services

2. Budget allocations specific to Auror platform implementation
2a. Documentation of federal/state grants used to fund Auror-related expenditures

3. Training manuals, guides, or protocols for Auror platform use by task force members
3a. Video recordings of Auror software training sessions
3b. Email communications regarding training schedules or materials

4. All incident reports, intelligence briefings, or case files generated through Auror's platform
4a. Spreadsheets/databases tracking organized retail crime incidents processed via Auror
4b. Performance metrics/reports evaluating Auror's effectiveness (2022-2024)

5. Records of technical malfunctions, data inaccuracies, or security breaches involving Auror
5a. Formal complaints from task force members or partner agencies about Auror's system
5b. Internal audits or third-party assessments of Auror's compliance with state data laws

6. Emails/memos between AG staff and Auror representatives (June 23, 2022-present)
6a. Meeting minutes where Auror platform use was discussed
6b. Correspondence with federal partners (FBI, DHS) regarding Auror data sharing

These records are requested from June 23, 2022, to present; Electronic copies are preferred in their original formats wherever possible, and commonly readable formats such as pdf, mp4, png where conversion is required.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robin Monks

Please reference that number on any future correspondence regarding this request. You requested the following: Records related to the Organized Retail Crime Theft Task Force announced on June 23, 2022, specifically concerning the implementation, use, and discussion of Auror's crime intelligence platform. 
1. All contracts, MOUs, RFPs, or service agreements between the AG's Office and Auror Inc. (auror.co) dated June 23, 2022, to present 
1a. Amendments, scope-of-work documents, or SLA agreements related to Auror's services 
1b. Invoices, payment receipts, or procurement documents for Auror software/services 
2. Budget allocations specific to Auror platform implementation 
2a. Documentation of federal/state grants used to fund Auror-related expenditures 
3. Training manuals, guides, or protocols for Auror platform use by task force members 
3a. Video recordings of Auror software training sessions 
3b. Email communications regarding training schedules or materials 
4. All incident reports, intelligence briefings, or case files generated through Auror's platform 
4a. Spreadsheets/databases tracking organized retail crime incidents processed via Auror 
4b. Performance metrics/reports evaluating Auror's effectiveness (2022-2024) 
5. Records of technical malfunctions, data inaccuracies, or security breaches involving Auror 
5a. Formal complaints from task force members or partner agencies about Auror's system 
5b. Internal audits or third-party assessments of Auror's compliance with state data laws 
6. Emails/memos between AG staff and Auror representatives (June 23, 2022-present) 
6a. Meeting minutes where Auror platform use was discussed 
6b. Correspondence with federal partners (FBI, DHS) regarding Auror data sharing 
These records are requested from June 23, 2022, to present; Electronic copies are preferred in their original formats wherever possible, and commonly readable formats such as pdf, mp4, png where conversion is required.

 Kristin Young

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Records (Contracts, Audit Logs, SB 34, Communications) (Bellflower Public Safety Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I request the following records concerning any products, services, platforms, sensors, or data feeds of the following categories, whether currently used, previously used, piloted, trialed, or formally considered by this agency, for the period January 1, 2020 through August 19, 2026:

Automated license plate reader ("ALPR") and connected-camera systems — including but not limited to Flock Safety (Flock Group Inc.), Motorola Solutions / Vigilant Solutions (LEARN, PlateSearch), Genetec (AutoVu), Axon / Fusus, Rekor, Leonardo/ELSAG, Neology, and Digital Recognition Network (DRN);
Data-integration, analytics, and "real-time crime center" (RTCC) / "real-time awareness center" (RTAC) platforms — including but not limited to Peregrine Technologies (peregrine.io), Palantir, Fusus (Axon), SoundThinking, and any comparable platform that aggregates, links, or searches across agency data sources; and
Any product beyond ALPR cameras offered by the above vendors (e.g., Flock's Condor PTZ video, FlockOS, Nova, or other data-intelligence products; Peregrine's data-integration or AI/"safety flagging" modules).

Where a term below refers to a Flock-specific feature (e.g., "Organization Audit"), please read it to also request the equivalent record in any other vendor's system.
1. Contracts and procurement. All contracts, master services agreements, order forms, amendments, renewals, statements of work, quotes, proposals, purchase orders, invoices, and payment records with any vendor identified above, including any data-processing addenda / data-processing agreements (DPAs), memoranda of understanding (MOUs), and any competitive-bid waivers or sole-source justifications.
2. Vendor communications. All communications (email, text/SMS, letters, meeting notes, calendar invitations) between agency personnel and representatives of any vendor identified above (including the vendor's @flocksafety.com, @peregrine.io, or equivalent domains), concerning procurement, deployment, configuration, camera or sensor siting, pilot / early-access / free-trial programs, and any product beyond ALPR cameras.
3. Search and audit logs. The complete audit/usage logs showing each search or query, including — for Flock — the "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" logs (Flock Insights dashboard), and — for any RTCC / data-integration platform (e.g., Peregrine) — the user access and query logs. For each entry, please include all available metadata fields, e.g.: record ID, user name, organization/agency name, date/time of search, license plate or query terms, stated reason, case number, camera count, time frame searched, filters, search type, and any text/AI prompt. Please export in the system's native machine-readable format (CSV/XLSX), not as a PDF printout, and do not strip metadata fields.
4. Hotlist and NCIC configuration (commonly the most important item). Records sufficient to show the full hotlist configuration of any ALPR system, including a screenshot, screen capture, printout, or CSV of the hotlists the agency subscribes to. This specifically includes which FBI NCIC "topics" are enabled and, in particular, whether the "Immigration Violator" file / topic is enabled, and the date any such topic was enabled or disabled. Also include any custom hotlists created by the agency.
5. Data sharing and external / federal access. A list of all external entities with which data is shared or from which it is received, and the settings governing that sharing, including:

The agency's Flock network-sharing settings, and whether "National Lookup" and/or statewide lookup are enabled, with the dates access was granted, modified, or revoked;
All external agencies that can access this agency's data, and all agencies whose data this agency can access, with dates;
Specifically, any access by or sharing with federal agencies — ICE, CBP, HSI, ATF, FBI, DHS — including records of searches those agencies (or other agencies on their behalf) ran against this agency's data;
All MOUs, data-sharing agreements, and network-participation terms (e.g., with a fusion center such as NCRIC), and any restrictions placed on downstream use or re-dissemination.

6. California ALPR statutory records (SB 34 and amendments).

The record of access required by Civil Code § 1798.90.52;
The agency's current ALPR usage and privacy policy required by Civil Code § 1798.90.51 (and, if the agency is an ALPR end-user, its policy under § 1798.90.53);
The results of the annual audit of ALPR searches for compliance with the usage/privacy policy (Civil Code § 1798.90.53), including any assessment of whether non-hotlist data was purged within 30 days of collection;
Any records concerning use of ALPR for immigration-enforcement geolocation or retention beyond 30 days (see Civ. Code § 1798.90.5 et seq., as amended).

7. Camera / sensor deployment and locations. Records sufficient to show the number, type, and locations of all cameras or sensors installed in the jurisdiction (fixed ALPR, mobile ALPR, PTZ/video, gunshot-detection, or other), their installation dates, and any encroachment, right-of-way, or other permits issued for their installation.
8. Data sources integrated into any data-integration / RTCC platform. For any platform identified above (e.g., Peregrine), a list of all data sources, feeds, and databases integrated into or accessible through the platform — for example computer-aided dispatch (CAD), records management systems (RMS), body-worn and in-car camera footage, fixed/traffic/school cameras, ALPR data, jail/booking data, DMV or state databases, and any third-party or commercial data sources — together with any system-configuration or data-source inventory documents.
9. Retention, governance, and training. Records reflecting data-retention periods and deletion practices, access controls (who is authorized to search and what approvals are required), prohibited uses, training materials, and internal policies, standard operating procedures, directives, or general orders governing use of any system identified above.
10. Misuse, breaches, and oversight. Any audits, reports, internal-affairs records, complaints, disciplinary records, or communications concerning suspected or confirmed misuse of any system (including searches for personal, immigration, or reproductive-health-related reasons), and any records of data breaches or security incidents involving the data.
11. Surveillance-use policy and impact reports. Any Surveillance Use Policy, Surveillance Impact Report, Privacy Impact Assessment / Data Protection Impact Assessment, or comparable document required by any applicable local surveillance-oversight ordinance, relating to ALPR, RTCC, or data-integration technology generally or to a specific vendor.
12. Governing-body review. Staff reports, resolutions, meeting agendas, minutes, and presentations to the city council / board of supervisors / oversight body concerning approval, funding, or renewal of any contract identified above.
13. Confirmation of non-use. If the agency has never used, piloted, or contracted for any ALPR, connected-camera, RTCC, or data-integration system of the kind described above, please confirm that in writing.

Format, preservation, and processing

Machine-readable format. Please provide records in their original electronic, machine-readable format with metadata intact (Gov. Code § 7922.570); spreadsheets and logs as CSV/XLSX, not PDF printouts.
Preservation. Because some responsive records (particularly ALPR search/audit logs) may be subject to short retention or automatic deletion, I request that the agency preserve all responsive records — and suspend any automatic purge of responsive audit logs — pending completion of this request.
Segregability and exemption log. If any record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify each record and the specific exemption claimed (Gov. Code § 7922.540), and release all reasonably segregable portions (Gov. Code § 7922.525). Data describing how the system operates and is used — as distinct from information about a specific individual — is generally not exempt investigative material (see ACLU of S. Cal. v. Superior Court (2017) 3 Cal.5th 1032). Personal information may be redacted while still disclosing system-level records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Christian Whitney

communications.communication:
Thank you for the October 14 response and the records in the pick-up folder. I've reviewed them, and the request is not yet complete. Many of its numbered items received no determination, and several records that the produced documents refer to were not included. Please reopen PRA 26-627 and provide a supplemental response on the points below.

1. Items that received no determination

Gov. Code § 7922.535(a) requires the City to state whether it has responsive records for each part of a request. The response did not address the following items, and I ask the City to either produce records or state in writing that none exist:

- Item 3: search and audit logs for PlateRanger or any other ALPR system.
- Item 6: the record of access under Civ. Code § 1798.90.52, the ALPR usage and privacy policy under § 1798.90.51 or .53, and any annual audit results.
- Item 8: data sources integrated into any platform. SoundThinking's proposal (in the Sept. 22, 2025 packet) refers to Motorola CommandAware and Axon Fusus as products "currently used by the City." Please confirm whether the City uses either one.
- Item 9: retention, access-control, and training policies, and any procedures or general orders.
- Item 10: misuse, complaint, or breach records.
- Item 11: any surveillance use policy or impact assessment.
- Item 13: confirmation of non-use. The July 14, 2025 staff report refers to "15 already functioning ALPR's deployed in the City." Please identify the vendor of those cameras and produce records responsive to Items 1–12 for them. If the City has never contracted with or piloted Flock Safety, please confirm that in writing.

2. Specific records referenced in the production but not produced

- The fully executed Agreement File No. 1097, including the executed MSA and addenda. The packet copy has blank signature lines, and the September 23, 2025 email says the agreement would be routed by DocuSign.
- The PlateRanger pilot MOU or evaluation agreement that Mr. McNerney said he submitted on May 22, 2025.
- The attachments to the July 24, 2025 "Coverage Definition Call" thread, including "ALPR Locations (1).kmz" and the ShotSpotter coverage KML file, in native format.
- Installation dates for each camera and sensor, plus the encroachment or right-of-way permits issued for them (Item 7). Only the permit-request emails were produced.
- The locations of ShotSpotter sensors on private property. Only government sites were produced.
- Purchase orders and payment records (Item 1).
- Minutes, resolutions, and presentation materials for the July 14 and September 22, 2025 council items (Item 12).

3. Records the City controls through its vendor

Referring Items 4 and 5 to the Sheriff's Department does not cover the City's own PlateRanger system. I have a separate request pending with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, but that request does not relieve the City of its obligation to produce records within its own possession or control.

Under Addendum Two, § 5.C of the City's agreement, "Customer shall own the PlateRanger Operational Data." The City is the contracting customer, and its Director of Public Safety administers the account. Records the City owns or has a contractual right to obtain are public records under Gov. Code § 7920.530 even when a vendor stores them (see City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017) 2 Cal.5th 608). Please obtain from SoundThinking and produce:

- the PlateRanger audit and search logs;
- the hotlist and NCIC topic configuration, including whether any immigration-related topic is enabled;
- the City's participation status in the Rekor Partner Sharing Network, with dates;
- the list of agencies that can access or have accessed the City's data.

If the City believes it lacks possession or control of these records, please explain why.

4. Withheld records

The response says certain records were withheld as attorney-client privileged. Please identify each one by date, author, recipients, and general subject, so the claim can be evaluated, and release any reasonably segregable portions (Gov. Code § 7922.525). Communications that included SoundThinking personnel are not privileged. Please also provide the names and titles of the persons responsible for the denial, as § 7922.540 requires.

5. Format and preservation

Please produce logs and data in their native machine-readable format (CSV or XLSX) under Gov. Code § 7922.570. Please also confirm that the City has preserved responsive audit logs and suspended any automatic deletion while this request is pending, as asked in my original request.

title: Bruce Sundlun

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Bruce Sundlun
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records, specifically those unreleased, mentioning or describing Bruce G. Sundlun (born: January 19, 1920 died: July 21, 2011), who was the former governor of Rhode Island.

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. Please search HQ records as well as ALL field offices and resident agencies.

If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

I am a member of the news media and request classification as such. I have previously written about the government and its activities, and am currently a reporter of The Boston Globe.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Alexa Gagosz
